newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 8.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--A veil of secrecy has been drawn over the government's tactics in its imminent talks with unions and employers over changes in the job market and labour relations. An inter-ministerial committe meeting yesterday pledged to keep the government's final positions under wraps to avert adverse reactions from unionists - who are already threatening a boycott - and to avoid incidents like last weekend's, in which protestors threw yoghurt at the labour and merchant marine ministers.

--Following a meeting with Deputy Foreign Minister George Papandreou, Italy's deputy foreign minister said Rome and Athens were in agreement on the general form that the multinational protection force to Albania would take. Press reports say that a Greek officer will be based in Tirana and there will be a Greek presence in the south.

--The recent spate of drug-related deaths on the streets of Athens and Thessaloniki has led the Greek and Turkish parliaments to decide on the creation of standing inter-parliamentary committee to combat drug trafficking.

--Police said meanwhile that the lethal combination of heroin and pills or alcohol was to blame for the surprisingly high number of recent deaths. Fifty-eight people have died since the beginning of the year.

--Investigators will examine the black box of an Olympic Airways Boeing that swerved off the runway as it prepared for take-off from Athens airport yesterday. On board were 150 passengers, including 12 Eurodeputies, destined for Strasbourg and Brussels. No one was injured in the incident.
--The impressive rise in the dollar on international markets is not expected to adversely affect the Greek economy.
--The fall in interest rates has forced investors to seek better returns elsewhere: heading the list are mutual funds, property investment and shares.

--The Cyprus issue cannot be solved by yesterday's methods, former German foreign minister Hans Dietrich Genscher says. "Cyprus cannot be held hostage by its divided status," he said, stressing that the European Union must find solutions.
--The finance ministry has issued a circular drastically cutting back on overtime work in the public sector and, in some cases, abolishing extra pay altogether.
--A six-year-old Greek girl took second prize at the 9th Biennale of Children's Art in Japan, beating out 56,000 other competitors from 132 countries.

--Negotiations between the government and workers at banks and public utilities and organisations (DEKOs) have settled on wage increases and the calling off of threatened industrial action, reports say.

--Women's organisations and high-profile activists, including Margaret Papandreou, the former wife of late ruling PASOK president and founder Andreas Papandreou, came out in support of shipping magnate George Ventouris's former wife in a hotly-contested custody battle.
